judgments.title: RUGAYAH BINTI MOHAMED & ors v HSBC AMANAH MALAYSIA BERHAD
judgments.catchwords: Interim Preservation Threshold for Financial Assets – Order 29 rule 4 Rules of Court 2012 – Order for sale of movable property – Statutory threshold – Interlocutory mandatory relief – Preservation of status quo – Whether a market-linked financial asset (such as investment units) experiencing normal market volatility and fluctuations satisfies the legal threshold of being property of a "perishable nature" or property "likely to deteriorate if kept" under Order 29 rule 4(1)(a) or (b) of the Rules of Court 2012. judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya & ors v RAMIZUL AMIN BIN HAMZAH
judgments.catchwords: RAYUAN JENAYAH - Kesalahan seksual terhadap kanak-kanak - s 14(a) Akta Kesalahan-Kesalahan Seksual Terhadap Kanak-Kanak 2017 - Dua pertuduhan - Sabitan - Keterangan saksi kanak-kanak - Kredibiliti SP5 - Percanggahan dan kelompangan material - Kelewatan laporan polis - Keterangan sokongan - Kes prima facie - Maksud seksual - Pembelaan Perayu - Sama ada pembelaan telah dipertimbangkan - Sama ada sabitan selamat - Hukuman - Rayuan silang Pendakwa Raya - Hukuman nyata tidak mencukupi atau nyata berlebihan - Faktor mitigasi dan pemberatan - Prinsip one transaction rule - Hukuman penjara - Serentak atau berturutan. Diputuskan, rayuan Perayu terhadap sabitan ditolak. Walau bagaimanapun, rayuan berhubung hukuman dibenarkan setakat hukuman penjara tiga (3) tahun bagi setiap pertuduhan diperintahkan berjalan secara serentak dan bukannya berturutan. Rayuan silang Pendakwa Raya ditolak. Perintah-perintah lain yang dibuat oleh Mahkamah Sesyen dikekalkan; Perayu merayu terhadap sabitan atas dua pertuduhan di bawah seksyen 14(a) Akta Kesalahan-Kesalahan Seksual Terhadap Kanak-Kanak 2017 dengan mencabar kredibiliti SP5, percanggahan dan kelompangan dalam keterangan pendakwaan, kelewatan membuat laporan polis serta kegagalan mengambil kira pembelaannya. Mahkamah mendapati keterangan SP5 adalah konsisten dalam perkara material dan percanggahan yang dibangkitkan tidak menjejaskan kredibilitinya. Mahkamah turut berpuas hati bahawa pihak Pendakwaan telah membuktikan semua elemen pertuduhan, termasuk bahawa perbuatan tersebut dilakukan bagi maksud seksual, dan pembelaan Perayu telah dipertimbangkan sewajarnya. Sabitan dikekalkan. Berhubung hukuman, hukuman penjara tiga tahun bagi setiap pertuduhan dikekalkan, tetapi diperintahkan berjalan secara serentak.
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Kuldeep Kumar a/l Jamna Dass

judgments.catchwords: CONTRACT: Formation – Contract with public authority – Forestry – Application for replacement logging area in permanent reserved forest – Approval letters issued by State Forestry Department – Approval expressed to be "in principle" and subject to conditions precedent – Express reservation of Director's right to amend or cancel approved area involving environmentally sensitive land – Applicant paid timber premium and fees pursuant to approval – Department acknowledged receipts would be attached "to the licence" – No licence in Form 1 ever issued – No agreement drafted, negotiated or executed – Whether approval letters and payments gave rise to a valid and binding contract – Whether rights in respect of forest produce could arise otherwise than by licence under the statutory scheme – Whether formal written contract was required to bind the Government – Whether cancellation of approval amounted to breach of contract – National Forestry Act 1984, ss 14, 15(1), 16, 19 – Government Contracts Act 1949, ss 2, 3. ADMINISTRATIVE LAW: Legitimate expectation – Exercise of statutory discretion – Cancellation of approval in principle for logging area – Applicant relied on long course of dealings and department's established practice of issuing licence once approval given and payments made – Approval expressly conditional and subject to reserved power of cancellation – District Forest Office report identified risk of erosion and downstream water pollution affecting eco-park and water treatment plant but recommended no objection subject to conditions – Whether doctrine of legitimate expectation could be invoked in private law action for damages in contract and tort – Whether legitimate expectation could arise from a conditional and qualified representation – Whether doctrine could fetter express statutory discretion – Whether Director bound to follow recommendation of subordinate office – Whether cancellation was within reserved power and supported by rational environmental grounds – Whether payment of premium conferred any vested right – Whether applicant remained free to nominate alternative area. TORT: Misfeasance in public office – Elements – Mala fide – State Director of Forestry cancelled approval after applicant had made payments – Applicant relied on timing of cancellation, absence of contemporaneous documentation, departure from District Forest Office's recommendation and allegedly inconsistent treatment of adjoining allocation – Whether targeted malice, knowledge of unlawfulness or reckless indifference was proved – Whether inference of bad faith could be drawn from surrounding circumstances amounting to suspicion and speculation – Whether Director was entitled to statutory protection – Vicarious liability – Whether State Forestry Department and State Government could be vicariously liable where personal liability of officer was not established – National Forestry Act 1984, s 106 – Government Proceedings Act 1956, ss 5, 6.

judgments.catchwords: Contract Law — Agreement to Build and Rent — Manufacturing facility development on industrial land — Tenant’s premature termination of build-and-rent agreement — Failure to obtain planning permission (Kebenaran Merancang or KM Approval) within agreed timeline — Whether contractual deadline constituted essential condition — Waiver and election by conduct — Tenant’s continued affirmation of contract after expiry of deadline — Requirement to give reasonable notice to reinstate time as being of the essence — Whether termination valid — Whether termination amounted to repudiatory breach. Contract Law — Waiver and Election — Expiry of contractual deadline for obtaining planning approval — Subsequent confirmation of revised project schedule extending performance period — Continued negotiations, approval of plans and specifications and participation in project implementation — Whether conduct inconsistent with intention to terminate — Whether right to terminate waived — Effect of non-waiver clause. Contract Law — Time of the Essence — Original deadline for obtaining planning permission not met — Contract affirmed after deadline — Whether fresh reasonable notice required before reliance on delay as ground for termination — Failure to reinstate time as being of the essence — Validity of termination. Contract Law — Repudiation — Wrongful termination by tenant — Landlord’s rejection of repudiation pursuant to s 40 Contracts Act 1950 — Whether agreement remained valid and subsisting — Attribution of responsibility for project failure. Contract Law — Variation Works — Additional construction works requested by tenant — Pits and trenches — Agreed additional costs — Partial payment made — Outstanding balance unpaid — Whether liability to pay survived subsequent contractual dispute. Damages — Agreed Liquidated Damages — Premature termination by tenant before commencement of tenancy — Clause providing for payment equivalent to rental for unexpired initial term — Whether enforceable — Application of principles in Cubic Electronics Sdn Bhd (In Liquidation) v Mars Telecommunications Sdn Bhd — Burden on defaulting party to establish unreasonableness. Damages — Prevention Principle — Non-occurrence of tenancy commencement date caused by tenant’s own wrongful termination — Whether tenant entitled to rely on non-fulfilment of condition to avoid agreed liquidated damages. Deposits — Rental Deposit — Contractual forfeiture upon premature termination by tenant — Whether forfeiture valid and enforceable — Absence of evidence that forfeiture was excessive, unconscionable or disproportionate. Damages — Construction and Reinstatement Costs — Reinstatement of pits and trenches following abandonment of project — Whether recoverable as foreseeable consequence of breach — Assessment of loss based on best available evidence. Restitution — Total Failure of Consideration — Claim for recovery of rental deposit and monies paid for variation works — Whether consideration wholly failed — Substantial performance of agreed works — Whether restitutionary claim sustainable. Planning Law — Town and Country Planning Act 1976, s 19(1) — Construction activities undertaken before planning approval obtained — Whether absence of planning permission rendered underlying contract illegal, void or unenforceable — Distinction between regulatory non-compliance and contractual enforceability. Guarantee and Indemnity — Construction of instrument — Guarantee securing tenant’s obligations under build-and-rent arrangement — Whether liability confined to tenancy period — Meaning of “Outstanding Sum” and agreed liquidated damages — Distinction between guarantee and indemnity under Contracts Act 1950 — Scope of indemnifier’s primary obligation. Guarantee and Indemnity — Enforcement against guarantor/indemnifier — Premature termination by principal debt

judgments.catchwords: Criminal Justice - Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, ss. 2, 37(d), 39B(1)(a) — Trafficking — Appeal against conviction — Whether statutory presumption of deemed possession under s. 37(d) can be conflated with substantive trafficking under s. 2 by "keeping and storing" without proof of an independent positive overt act beyond reasonable doubt — Presumption stacking and impermissible inversion of burden of proof — Criminal Procedure Code, s. 180(3) — Duty of trial court to amend charge to possession under s. 39A(2) where only s. 37(d) possession proved at close of prosecution case — Mid-trial mutation of case causing incurable prejudice and breach of natural justice — Evidence Act 1950, s. 54(1) — Prejudicial reception of bad character evidence (AADK document and smoking bong) — Break in chain of custody via non-contemporaneous, post-facto reconstruction of Drug Exhibit Register (POL 260) compromising identity of dangerous drugs — Non-exclusive access to ancestral premises and negative forensic nexus — Curative provisions inapplicable where foundational evidence of possession is fatally tainted — Conviction quashed and substituted conviction under s. 39A(2) refused — Accused acquitted and discharged.
